title: Why Proper Drain Slope Matters
description: Horizontal drainage pipes rely on gravity to move liquid waste and suspended solids together efficiently. Maintaining the correct slope, as defined by local plumbing codes, ensures proper scouring velocity. If the pipe slope is too flat, flow velocity drops, allowing solids to settle out and form blockages. Conversely, if the slope is excessively steep, liquids drain rapidly while solids fall out of suspension and stick to the pipe wall. Always verify your local code requirements and use a precise torpedo level during installation to maintain steady, self-cleaning gravity flow.
